meta.method: Pass 1: news-first wet-season sweep (Apr–Nov) as Task 26. Pass 2 (Task 28): recall queries — Anadolu/Reuters/AFP/Al Jazeera/Xinhua, ReliefWeb, Dartmouth Flood Observatory, death/cause phrases with no site: filter, official Lagos/NIHSA sites, and out-of-season Jan–Mar and Dec. Qualifying reports name a Lagos State place and a date, and describe water on streets or in homes. Quotes ≤25 words, verbatim. Flood date is the flood day, not publication day.
notes: 15 districts are the largest LGAs by typical census/population rank, not neighbourhoods. Lekki/Ajah searched under Eti-Osa.
Premium Times full text was blocked on fetch; 2019 Badagry and Isheri pieces were screened from titles/snippets only and not kept without a readable flood day.
X accounts of LASEMA, Lagos MoE and NEMA: no dated 2019 flood posts reached.
Nairaland/YouTube treated as leads only; none independently confirmed a new flood day.
Pass 2 added 2026-10-18. Existing pass-1 reports tagged pass=1; new reports tagged pass=2.
Anadolu 23 Oct 2019 (6 dead, Oyan Dam) found via site:aa.com.tr teaser then the article URL; Punch original found via "Lagos flood" killed / six-killed query.

areas: Ogudu end of the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway
reports.impacts: Early-morning rain lasting more than one hour in some places flooded several roads; traffic slow on major roads; trees uprooted on Alfred Rewane Road, Ikoyi, falling on moving cars.
reports.quote: Floods have taken over parts of Lagos State following an early morning heavy rainfall.
reports.cause_quote: Floods have taken over parts of Lagos State following an early morning heavy rainfall.

reports.impacts: About two hours of rain from around 9.30am; two buildings partially collapsed in Abule Egba and Ladipo; trees fell in Ikoyi, Alausa, Ikeja GRA and Agege Motor Road. LASEMA GM Adesina Tiamiyu: no life lost.
reports.quote: Many residents of the two states could not go about their daily businesses as a result of flood that accompanied the heavy rainfall.
reports.cause_quote: What we had around Lagos today (Monday) were the wreckages of the heavy rain and windstorm.

reports.impacts: About two hours of rain from about 8:35 a.m.; flood made major roads impassable and went into homes and offices; at Agric, Ikorodu, water on the road to Asolo in Isawo was knee-high.
reports.quote: The flood in some parts of the city left thousands of residents stranded as it made many major roads impassable and went into living homes.
reports.cause_quote: mass of plastics and nylons washed out from blocked drains littered the streets

reports.impacts: Resident Gbolahan Soaga trapped 8am–1pm between Alausa Secretariat and old toll gate / Motorways–7up; turned back because the estate at Alapere and Ogudu ends was flooded.
reports.quote: This was because of the downpour that made the Estate at Alapere and Ogudu ends flooded.
reports.cause_quote: I believe the problem is largely drainage.

reports.impacts: Monday morning downpour submerged vehicles, tricycles and motorcycles; several broke down in the flood from Ojuwoye Market to Idi-Oro and Moshalashi.
reports.quote: Many vehicles, tricycles and motorcycles were on Monday morning submerged in flood at Mushin, Agege Motor Road, Lagos.
reports.cause_quote: submerged in flood at Mushin, Agege Motor Road, Lagos, following an early morning downpour

reports.impacts: Correspondents on Monday reported flash floods across major areas; ceaseless downpour for seven days last week and this week. Knee-deep water between Ejigbo LCDA and Access Bank on Ikotun road. At vulcanizer bus stop, Akowonjo Road, Egbeda, water sometimes takes two days to disappear and enters houses.
reports.quote: flash floods were experienced in major areas in Ikeja, Agege, Ikorodu, Iju, Obalende, Lekki, Badagry, Ojodu, among hundreds of other areas in Lagos.
reports.cause_quote: The immediate past government abandoned the construction of the Isawo road, thus leaving the road with no drainage by the sides.

reports.impacts: Photo report of Agege communities after rainfall; named streets/areas shown flooded.
reports.quote: A community of Agege Local Government Area, Lagos state after rainfall.

reports.impacts: Heavy rainfall from about 8 am submerged an Agege community and trapped pupils in Ladoje Nursery and Primary School; motorists and commuters trapped in traffic; Yaba road flooded.
reports.quote: A community in Agege Local Government Area of Lagos State, was submerged in flood water, trapping some students in a Nursery and Primary school.
reports.cause_quote: following the persistent heavy downpour yesterday

reports.impacts: Overnight rain from about 2:15 am, full force by 3:15 am; canal overflowed. An 11-year-old boy and rescuer Wasiu ('Wasiu Stubborn') swept into the Aboru–Iyana-Ipaja canal on Ige Road. Furniture maker Gift Wejem said flood had swept away furniture, materials, machines and a generator when the canal overflowed.
reports.quote: This rain started almost four or five days ago but the one of last night was one of the heaviest.
reports.cause_quote: It is the bad road and narrow culvert that caused these deaths
reports.cause_who: Suleiman Adedokun, shop owner beside the canal

deaths.who_reported: Suleiman Adedokun, shop owner beside the canal
deaths.quote: the flood swept away an 11-year-old boy and his rescuer, one Wasiu into a canal

reports.impacts: Same Saturday canal overflow as r2019-009: 11-year-old boy and rescuer Wasiu swept into the canal.
reports.quote: residents of Aboru and Iyana-Ipaja in the Alimosho area of Lagos on Saturday as the flood swept away an 11-year-old boy and his rescuer
reports.cause_quote: This flat culvert cannot contain water.
reports.cause_who: Solomon Agboghoroma, Community Development Association leader, Oki town

deaths.who_reported: Suleiman Adedokun, shop owner beside the canal
deaths.quote: the flood swept away an 11-year-old boy and his rescuer, one Wasiu into a canal

reports.impacts: Correspondents monitored Friday–Sunday. Saturday: Magodo building collapse (Jumiah Utache and three children — collapse, not a flood drowning); Aboru boy and Wasiu; landlord Aina Oke, Abule Egba, fence collapsed on two SUVs. Lekki flood covered at least 1.4 km on Bola Ahmed Tinubu Avenue and Bogije. Four vehicles trapped on Agric-Isawo Road. Awoyaya residents walked through flood. Gridlock and destroyed homes at Jakande, Lekki, Ebute-Meta, Ijegun, Idimu, Agege, Randle and Maryland.
reports.quote: The flood also caused gridlock and destroyed homes at Jakande, Lekki, Ebute-Meta, Ijegun, Idimu, Agege, Randle and Maryland areas of Lagos State.
reports.cause_quote: It was learnt that the flood in Lekki was caused by poor drainage system.

deaths.quote: the flood had claimed the lives of a 11-year-old boy, and a man, identified, as Wasiu

reports.impacts: BBC Pidgin: non-stop heavy rain, flood everywhere; two buildings collapsed (Magodo and Ita Elewa, Ikorodu); four dead in Magodo collapse (mother, two children, sister) per LASEMA. Some people said rain plus flood contributed to collapse; LASEMA also cited construction/stress on the Ikorodu mud-brick building.
reports.quote: heavy rain wey fall non-stop make plenti flood full everi wia
reports.cause_quote: Heavy rain bin fall well-well for Lagos and dis cause serious flooding

reports.impacts: Second weekend in a row: residents trapped in homes and hours in traffic after hours of downpour on Sunday. State had warned Friday that flood in Ikoyi, Victoria Island and other parts could last the weekend because of Oyan Dam release.
reports.quote: residents of Lagos State were trapped in their homes and some others spent hours in traffic as a result of the flood
reports.cause_quote: the lagoon cannot discharge and is causing back flow into drainage outlets
reports.cause_who: Tunji Bello, Commissioner for Environment and Water Resources

reports.impacts: Rain from about 2 am Sunday into the evening; several communities taken over by flood; residents trapped in homes; traffic gridlock. Photo: flood on Ikotun-Egbeda road. Discovery Estate / Opic Isheri (Lagos–Ogun border) also described; not listed as a Lagos place.
reports.quote: several communities were completely taken over by heavy flood, leaving many residents trapped in their homes
reports.cause_quote: Following torrential rainfall across Lagos State, yesterday, several communities were completely taken over by heavy flood

areas: Community Road, Ago Palace Way, Isolo
reports.impacts: Flood on Community Road, Ago Palace Way, distressed residents, shop owners and commuters. Photo caption: motorists wading through flood at Agege Motor Road by Total filling station yesterday.
reports.quote: The bad drainage system is the main reason for this flooding. There is nowhere for the water to go out
reports.cause_quote: The flood, which is a result of the persistent rainfall and bad drainage system in the community

reports.impacts: Reporter visit Friday: Ogun River over banks into homes. Last few weeks of rain; water constant more than one week. Bathroom and toilets unusable at one house because water took the area and sewage flowed backward. Recently abandoned houses. Photo of flooding at Irawo, Ikorodu road.
reports.quote: homes around some of these areas were already flooded, with no end in sight
reports.cause_quote: In the last few weeks, as a result of the incessant rains, residents of certain Lagos communities have experienced serious flooding.

reports.impacts: Hundreds of communities and estates in parts of Lagos and Ogun submerged after heavy downpour and opening of Oyan Dam. Ketu and Mile 12 flooded in the last one week. As of Sunday afternoon, flood around Long Bridge almost overflowing. Commissioner: lagoon could not discharge; back flow into drainage.
reports.quote: Hundreds of communities and estates in parts of Lagos and Ogun states have been submerged by flood
reports.cause_quote: the lagoon could not discharge water and had caused back flow into drainage outlets
reports.cause_who: Tunji Bello, Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources

reports.impacts: Houses, shops and places of worship submerged after Oyan Dam release. Tour Monday. Six deaths as named by residents: Baba Ibeji, Baba Michael, an unidentified Egun man (three drowned Monday night when canoes hit debris/hyacinth at Kio-Kio; bodies not found); a woman bitten by a snake while boarding a floater at Unity Estate, Owode-Onirin; a mother and baby who drowned when a canoe to Maidan-Orile capsized (bodies recovered three days later). Residents using canoes; schools shut.
reports.quote: The recent release of water from the Oyan Dam in Abeokuta has plunged residents of some communities in Lagos into untold hardship
reports.cause_quote: Debris and water hyacinth around the Itowolo Bridge have affected the flow of water out of the communities.

deaths.who_reported: Precious Okolie, trader; Chekwube Nuanya, helmsman; Mrs Agbaje, resident
deaths.quote: alleged that some persons had drowned in the flood water

reports.impacts: At least six people killed in floods in Lagos, citing Punch: three men, two women and a baby. Houses and shops submerged; businesses paralysed; schools shut; many fled. Blamed on recent Oyan Dam release in Abeokuta. Ogun-Osun River Basin Authority confirmed release because the dam filled from heavy downpours.
reports.quote: At least six people were killed in floods in the Nigerian city of Lagos, local media reported on Wednesday.
reports.cause_quote: The floods were caused by a recent release of water from the Oyan Dam in Abeokuta

deaths.quote: At least six people were killed in floods in the Nigerian city of Lagos, local media reported on Wednesday.

reports.impacts: Photo report of ongoing inundation: cars submerged, houses with stagnant water, shops shut, school locked, residents using canoes. Called the worst recent flooding; neighbouring communities had recovered.
reports.quote: Cars have been submerged, houses filled with stagnant water while business places have been shut.

reports.impacts: Residents said lives and property lost and they were sacked from homes and businesses. NTIC closed five weeks; Golden Silk International shut over four weeks; a diaper factory shut; Lasena Waters shut three weeks. Students missed school. Describes 2019 floodwaters covering a greater area than 2018 along the Ogun River.
reports.quote: while the community has lost lives and property, and have been sacked from their homes and businesses
reports.cause_quote: whose properties had been flooded by the release of water from the Oyan Dam
reports.cause_who: Abayomi Akinde, Chairman, Riverview Estate Residents and Stakeholders Association
reports.review_note: 2026-10-18 reviewer: article names no flood day or week (roundup / ongoing inundation); date_confidence set to period; date is the publication date.
